items.title: Tell your care team about low readings
items.text: You had low sugar readings 10.3% of the time, which can make you feel shaky or dizzy, so share this with your team before your next visit.

items.title: Take a short walk after meals
items.text: Your sugar rose about 13.1 mg/dL less after meals when you walked. Aim for 10 to 20 minutes after dinner, where the program saw the biggest gain (18.3 mg/dL). A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a fifth of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet. Because of your low readings, check with your care team before walking more. Walk after eating, not on an empty stomach, carry juice or glucose tablets, and stop to check your sugar if you feel shaky, sweaty or confused.

rejected.text: Walking after meals helped your sugar rise 13.1 mg/dL less, so try walking 10 to 20 minutes after dinner, but check with your care team first.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Having dinner at 8 pm or later, which happened 66.7% of the time, is linked to sugar rising 9.2 mg/dL more, so try to eat dinner before 8 pm.

items.title: Hold off on longer fasts for now
items.text: Your overnight fast currently averages 12.4 hours, but check with your care team before making any changes, especially since you had low sugar readings 10.3% of the time.
